C2.rationale: Level 1 anchor: appraisal of quality appears in outcomes - evaluating model performance against community-recognised metrics, critically assessing the outcomes of data analysis, and reflecting on one's contribution to the team - but no named core assessment item is a criterion-referenced appraisal task. C3.rationale: Level 2 requires core units to address AI capabilities AND limitations/ethics with use-with-limits discussed AND assessed. Ethics and data-risk content is documented only as unit outcomes (CITS4009, CITS2402) and as capstone lecture content; no named assessment item in any unit covers AI limitations, ethics or governance, and the extract never enumerates the compulsory 30-point group, so none of these units is shown to be core. The units that carry explicit AI ethics and critique (PHIL1001, PHIL2008, SCIE2100) appear in the prescribed list as electives. That leaves the level-1 anchor: digital and AI content present as electives and as tool operation. Level 3 fails outright - no core assessment requires critique or governance of AI systems (bias, accountability, transparency, regulation, data governance) in the data-science context.

W1.rationale: Level 1 anchor: communication and professional conduct appear in outcomes - communicating model results to stakeholders in written, oral and visual form, and performing professionally in a team - and communication skills are taught in capstone lectures. Level 2 needs at least one core assessment in a recognised professional genre or addressed to an audience beyond the teaching team, judged against criteria drawn from practice. The capstone's named assessment items are an individual essay, a group project deliverable and an individual project assessment, none identified as a client brief, consultancy advice, pitch or public-facing artefact; the external party is optional in the handbook's own wording ('an academic and/or industry mentor'), and no criterion drawn from professional practice is documented as applied by that party. Per R2 and Barrie, stated attributes do not lift the score.

Not level 3: such tasks are not documented as the program's assessment spine. The extract does not enumerate the compulsory 30-point group and shows no earlier scaffolding of end-to-end professional tasks; the assessment patterns visible across the prescribed units are mid-semester tests, laboratories, quizzes and final examinations.

W3.rationale: Level 1 anchor: work-situated learning exists in the prescribed unit list only as an optional internship. The McCusker Centre for Citizenship Internship carries 100 hours of work with supervisor evaluation and assessed reflection, but the handbook records it as awarded through a competitive application process, and the course structure places compulsory study in a 30-point 'Take all units' group with the remainder in elective groups. The other internship units in the prescribed list restrict entry to other courses - the Computer Science WIL Internship to the Bachelor of Advanced Computer Science or the Computer Science major, and the Work Integrated Learning Internship Program to Bachelor of Commerce, Business, Economics and named majors. Level 2 therefore fails: no core unit is documented as placing students in a real workplace or professional-community setting with practitioner supervision and assessment, and no in-practice route applies because the cohort is not documented as already practising. Not level 0, because work-integrated learning does appear in the course structure. The capstone is scored in W2, not here: it is an on-campus project unit, and simulation is excluded from W3.

ambiguities: Core membership is unresolvable from the extract. The course structure declares a compulsory group ('Take all units (30 points):') and three elective groups, but the capture returned the group headings with no unit lists, so the extract never says which of the 112 prescribed units are core. Every level-2 and level-3 anchor in C1-C4 and W1-W3 turns on the phrase 'core unit' or 'core assessment'. Resolved by accepting exactly one premise - that CITS5553 Data Science Capstone Project is required, because the handbook calls it 'the capstone unit CITS5553 Data Science Capstone Project in their final semester' for this course and gates it on enrolment in 62530 plus 66 points - and by treating every other unit's core status as unproven, which resolves each remaining item downward.

C1 straddled 1 and 2. The capstone's group project deliverable with separate individual project assessment satisfies level 2 only if the capstone is core; otherwise level 1 applies. Resolved to 2 on the single accepted premise above, and recorded here rather than propagated to other items.

C2 straddled 1 and 2. Evaluating model performance against metrics recognised by the data science community is criterion-referenced appraisal, but it is stated as an outcome and no named assessment item is an appraisal task. Resolved downward to 1 under the never-resolve-upward rule and R2.

C3 straddled 1 and 2. Ethics of data practice, data-breach risk and the social principles of large-scale data science projects are documented, satisfying the 'limitations/ethics' half of level 2, but only in outcomes and lecture content; level 2 also requires that use with limits be assessed, which no named assessment item shows. Resolved downward to 1.

C5 straddled 2 and 3. The research project pair documents inquiry design, execution and a staged supervised sequence, but level 3 requires the project to be REQUIRED rather than one route among several, and it is gated on a weighted average mark of at least 70 per cent. Resolved downward to 2.

W1 straddled 1 and 2. 'mentor/client meetings' suggests an audience beyond the teaching team, but the supervisor is documented as 'an academic and/or industry mentor', so an external party is optional, and no assessment item is named as a professional genre judged against practice criteria. Resolved downward to 1.

W3 versus W2 for the capstone.
